subject: Community Preservation Annual Public Hearing
overview: The committee held its annual public hearing to discuss project priorities and gather feedback on the Community Preservation Plan. Discussion focused on the role of CPA funds in leveraging larger grants for parks, the establishment of the Affordable Housing Trust, and ongoing historic cemetery preservation.

items.title: CPA Program Overview and 2024 Timeline
items.summary: Theresa Dupont presented an overview of the $2.5 million distributed in the previous fiscal year and outlined the 2024 application cycle, which opens on July 8.

items.title: Open Space and Recreation Planning
items.summary: Staff discussed the success of using CPA funds for park design and community outreach to secure larger state and federal construction grants, specifically citing the Carr Park model and upcoming needs for Playstead and Tufts Parks.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust Fund Update
items.summary: Housing Planner Aditi Moogoor introduced the new Affordable Housing Trust Fund, explaining its role in creating units and seeking future funding collaboration with the CPC.

items.title: Historic Preservation and Municipal Assets
items.summary: The committee reviewed the status of master planning for Oak Grove and Cross Street cemeteries and discussed future preservation needs for City Hall windows, fire stations, and the Curtis Tufts School.

items.title: Community Facility Needs and Hagner Center
items.summary: Members discussed the potential for a new recreation and social services hub at the Hagner Center and the ongoing need for secure archival storage for city records.

items.title: Dugger Park Tennis Court Memorial Signage
items.summary: The committee decided to install a fence sign for Clarence Roan and return the surplus $2,000 to CPA reserves after learning a memorial plaque for Roan already exists at the site.
